Dear Residents of Larkspur Lofts,

I’m writing to address concerns about the drone I flew from the roof deck on Saturday, October 31, around 4 p.m., and to explain what I was doing.

I’m Jess Okafor in Unit 5A, and I’ve lived here for three years. I work as a wedding photographer and was testing a new Halvard Mini 4 drone before photographing a vineyard wedding in Dundee. The flight lasted approximately 11 minutes. Throughout the flight, the camera was pointed west toward the river and the Fremont Bridge, not toward residents’ windows.

I understand that seeing a drone hovering over the courtyard, without knowing why it was there or what it was recording, could feel intrusive or unsettling. I’m sorry that my flight caused worry. I should have considered how it would look to neighbors and communicated beforehand.

Anyone who would like to see the full, unedited footage is welcome to do so. Please knock on my door at 5A or email me at jess.okafor@mailbox.example to arrange a time.

I also want to address the note posted in the lobby. While concerns about privacy are entirely reasonable, publicly identifying my unit and calling me a “creep” was hurtful and inappropriate. I hope we can raise concerns without personal insults or public accusations.

The current HOA rules do not address drones. I will ask the board to add the subject to the November 19 meeting agenda, at 7 p.m. in the community room, so residents can discuss clear expectations. I will not fly from the roof again until the board has decided on a rule.

If something I do raises a concern in the future, please speak with me directly rather than posting a note. I’m willing to listen, answer questions, and work toward a resolution that respects everyone’s privacy and comfort.

Sincerely,  
Jess Okafor  
Unit 5A
